punchline: Sethi is famously indifferent to the daily latte; his plan is to cut hard on the two biggest optional costs and spend freely on what you love.
thirty_sec: Ramit Sethi does not tell people to give up the daily latte. He points to five to ten big financial decisions, such as automating savings and negotiating salary. His Next $100 principle picks the two biggest discretionary expenses, his own being eating out and going out, and cuts them by 25 to 33 percent over six months. The cash goes to investing and travel, and what is left after automation is yours to spend.
